issues.legal_issue: For a statutory restoration proceeding protecting land held by a member of a protected tribal community, transfer includes the passage of possession to a non-member even without a transfer as defined by property-transfer legislation.
material_facts: The land had been held by a member of a Scheduled Tribe’s ancestor as a raiyat.
The transferee’s predecessor claimed that the land had been surrendered and resumed before conveying it, but failed to establish resumption.
The transferee’s claim to have acquired title by long possession was also not established.
The authorities ordered eviction under the statutory provision protecting tribal land, and the High Court held that the provision did not apply to this kind of transfer.
issues.conclusion: The statutory meaning of transfer is not confined to a transfer as defined by the Transfer of Property Act. Because possession passed from a person entitled to hold it to a non-member, the authorities could apply the protective provision; the High Court’s contrary decision was reversed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 71A of the Chhotanagpur Tenancy Act allows restoration where a transfer contravenes Section 46 or another provision of the Act, or occurs by a fraudulent method. Since Section 71A does not define transfer, its meaning should not be restricted to Section 5 of the Transfer of Property Act. In light of the protective purpose of Section 71A, transfer includes the physical passage of possession from a protected holder entitled to possess the land to a non-member. The Court applied the liberal-construction approach in Manchegowda v. State of Karnataka, Lingappa Pochanna Appelwar v. State of Maharashtra, Kamini Krishnayya v. Guraza Seshachalam, and D (a minor) v. Berkshire County Council.

rule.if: tribal_land_restoration_proceeding and protected_holder_entitled_to_possession and possession_passed_to_nonmember and transferor_failed_to_establish_resumption

predicates.tribal_land_restoration_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding to restore land under a statutory scheme protecting land held by members of a protected tribal community.
predicates.protected_holder_entitled_to_possession: A member of the protected community, or that member’s predecessor, was entitled to hold possession of the land.
predicates.possession_passed_to_nonmember: Possession of the land passed to a person who was not a member of the protected community.
predicates.transferor_failed_to_establish_resumptio: The person who purported to transfer the land failed to establish that the land had first been resumed from the protected holder.

issues.definition: When a restoration proceeding concerns land that a protected holder was entitled to possess, possession passed to a non-member, and the purported transferor did not establish resumption, the passage of possession falls within the protective restoration power.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee who has improved land subject to a statutory restoration order may be compensated for the improvements even though the transferee is to be evicted.
material_facts: The transferee had made improvements to the property.
The Court upheld the statutory authority’s decision to restore the land and ordered the Deputy Commissioner to value the improvements and fix compensation payable to the transferee.
issues.conclusion: The Deputy Commissioner was directed to assess the value of the improvements and fix compensation payable to the transferee, ensuring payment without making prior deposit a condition of dispossession.
issues.legal_principle: Although Section 71A provides for eviction without payment of compensation, the Court considered compensation for improvements appropriate on the facts of this case. It distinguished cases in which a transferee uses fraudulent methods to overreach the law and make improvements, where compensation may not be payable. The Court gave no broader rule or earlier case as the basis for this case-specific direction.

predicates.tribal_land_restoration_proceeding: The matter is a proceeding to restore land under a statutory scheme protecting land held by members of a protected tribal community.
predicates.transferee_made_property_improvements: The person subject to eviction made improvements to the property.

issues.definition: In a restoration proceeding, if the transferee made improvements to the property, compensation for those improvements may be ordered.
